claim_verdicts.evidence: "The direction of dependency within the application should be in the direction of abstraction, not implementation details." ... "implementation details can be written to depend on and implement higher-level abstractions, rather than the other way around." Lesson section 3 wording (high-level code depends on an abstraction, not a concrete low-level implementation) matches.

git show stage-1:samples/DonHang.Samples/Samples/Design/OrderNotifications.cs lines 9-23: `private readonly EmailNotifier notifier = new();`, `public sealed class OrderNotifications(INotifier notifier)`, both Handle bodies `notifier.Send(orderId, "order placed")`. Lesson block matches character-for-character.

git show stage-1:DonHang.Domain/OrderService.cs lines 6-23: `OrderService(IOrderRepository repository, INotifier notifier)`, PlaceOrderAsync calls `notifier.Send(order.Id, "order placed")`; no concrete notifier type named anywhere in the file. Lesson block matches.

DonHang.Domain/INotifier.cs: `namespace DonHang.Domain; public interface INotifier { void Send(int orderId, string subject); }`. DonHang.Infrastructure/LoggingNotifier.cs: `public sealed class LoggingNotifier(ILogger<LoggingNotifier> logger) : INotifier` whose Send calls `logger.LogInformation(...)`.

DonHang.Infrastructure.csproj: `<ProjectReference Include="..\DonHang.Domain\DonHang.Domain.csproj" />`. DonHang.Domain.csproj contains only a PropertyGroup: no ProjectReference (and no PackageReference).
"Three situations always produce an implicit reference conversion: ... assigning a reference type instance to a variable of an interface the type implements, ..."

Lesson now reads exactly the round-1 suggested_text: "if `Send` changed, `NotifierBase`, which implements it for `EmailNotifier` and `SmsNotifier`, would have to change too." Docs: "The class must provide an implementation for every member declared in the interface" (interfaces.md:35). stage-1 NotifierBase.cs declares Send; EmailNotifier/SmsNotifier only override Format. Round-1 scratch build (Send signature changed in INotifier + NotifierBase only) built with 0 errors.

Checked by inspection of the pattern in the lesson's own code: a class containing `new EmailNotifier()` names EmailNotifier in its source, so it cannot compile without that class and must be edited to use another one, whatever the field type. Consistent with docs: "compile-time dependency flows in the direction of runtime execution" unless the caller depends only on an abstraction.

Lesson now says "covered later in the dependency-injection module". track.yaml orders modules solid (design.l1.solid-dip line 261), layered, dependency-injection (line 394; design.l1.dependency-injection-intro line 403). Separation of principle and practice: "The practice of dependency injection is made possible by following the dependency inversion principle" (architectural-principles.md:46).

git grep 'interface INotifier' stage-1 -> exactly two: samples/DonHang.Samples/Samples/Oop/INotifier.cs:5 (namespace DonHang.Samples.Oop) and DonHang.Domain/INotifier.cs:5 (namespace DonHang.Domain); both declare only `void Send(int orderId, string subject);`. NotifierBase : INotifier (samples); LoggingNotifier : INotifier (Domain, via `using DonHang.Domain`). DonHang.Samples.csproj has no ProjectReference, so EmailNotifier cannot be converted to DonHang.Domain.INotifier.

issues.fix: Replace with: "a high-level class that creates its own `EmailNotifier` is tightly coupled in that lesson's sense: switching the channel forces a change in that class."
